1.referenceTitle: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/1891 on inorganic arsenic in fish and seafood
1.citation: European Commission. Regulation (EU) 2025/1891 of 17 September 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as regards maximum levels of inorganic arsenic in fish and other seafood. OJ L 2025/1891, 18 September 2025.
1.summary: The amendment adds wet-weight inorganic-arsenic maxima for specified fish and seafood, defines inorganic arsenic as As(III) plus As(V), and preserves separate total-arsenic treatment for salt. Species and edible-portion rules vary.
1.establishes: It entered into force on 8 October 2025. Covered seafood lawfully marketed earlier may remain until its durability or use-by date. The act sets legal values and scope; it does not itself prescribe a particular laboratory method in every case.
1.relevance: This is a binding concentration-limit event in HMTc’s watch. Comparisons need the correct aquatic species, tissue and wet-weight basis; the legal instrument does not validate the article’s aggregate count of equal or stricter HMTc cells.

evidence.note: Reused exact same-day source review from batch7-eu-deadlines.json ref 1. Read complete act, Articles 1–2 and Annex 3.4.5–3.4.9. Fish eaten whole use whole-fish results; Pecten maximus uses adductor and gonad; crustacean cephalothorax is excluded. Analytical workflow recommendations in the article are separate interpretation.

2.referenceTitle: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 on maximum levels of nickel in certain foodstuffs
2.citation: European Commission. Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 of 30 July 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as regards maximum levels of nickel in certain foodstuffs. OJ L 2024/1987, 31 July 2024.
2.summary: The amendment sets nickel maxima by food category. Most apply from 1 July 2025; cereal rows 3.6.11.1–3.6.11.5 apply from 1 July 2026. Infant cereal-based food is a separate row with the earlier date.
2.establishes: Food lawfully marketed before its applicable date can remain until its durability or use-by date. Therefore, the July 2026 application date does not end every transitional sale. Category, preparation, processing and dry/wet basis remain material.
2.relevance: This gives HMTc distinct category application dates rather than one nickel deadline. The cereal date has passed by this review, while lawful earlier stock may still qualify for transitional sale. It does not by itself verify all HMTc comparison cells.

evidence.note: Reused exact same-day source review from batch7-eu-deadlines.json ref 3. Read original Articles 1–2 and full Annex, refreshing same-day prior amendment research. Entry into force is the twentieth day after July 31 publication, distinct from adoption and application. Article 1 retains the durability/use-by exception. Editorial: “transition ended” is too absolute.

3.referenceTitle: NHC/SAMR Announcement No. 6 of 2025 publishing GB 2762-2025
3.citation: National Health Commission and State Administration for Market Regulation, China. Announcement No. 6 of 2025, publishing GB 2762-2025 and other national food-safety standards. Dated September 2, 2025; posted September 25, 2025. Supplemented by USDA FAS report CH2025-0202.
3.summary: The announcement formally publishes GB 2762-2025 among 32 standards and two amendments. The accompanying USDA translation identifies September 2, 2026 as the replacement standard’s effective date.
3.establishes: The announcement verifies adoption and identity; it does not print the effective date or numerical tables in its HTML. The reviewed translation is expressly unofficial. The 2025 standard is effective by this review date.
3.relevance: HMTc’s watch must now treat GB 2762-2025 as effective, with product-level comparisons to its own categories. The article’s future-tense and adopted-not-effective framing was tied to its August 2026 publication and is stale on September 15.

4.referenceTitle: ECHA proposes restrictions on chromium(VI) substances
4.citation: European Chemicals Agency. ECHA proposes restrictions on chromium(VI) substances to protect health. ECHA/NR/25/11, April 29, 2025. Supplementary process context: 2026 SEAC draft-opinion consultation.
4.summary: ECHA’s notice describes a proposed restriction of certain chromium(VI) substances, with exceptions for specified industrial uses meeting proposed exposure and emission conditions. It envisages replacing specified REACH authorization requirements, with a later decision by the Commission and Member States.
4.establishes: The 2025 notice is a proposal, not an adopted general prohibition. A 2026 consultation on the socio-economic draft opinion documents a later procedural stage. The complete latest dossier and final adoption status were not independently audited here.
4.relevance: This illustrates a proposal event in HMTc’s tracker. It supports monitoring substitution and supply-chain implications, not inserting a chromium(VI) food maximum or labeling all industrial uses already prohibited.

5.citation: US Food and Drug Administration. FDA’s Infant Formula Product Testing Results. FY 2023–2025 market-basket results, official results page accessed September 15, 2026.
5.summary: FDA reports testing 312 formula samples for arsenic, cadmium, lead and mercury and presents concentrations as prepared for feeding. It describes market-basket testing as a snapshot and states that its findings affirm formula safety.
5.establishes: Detecting a contaminant does not automatically establish harm. These monitoring results do not capture all variation among production lots and do not create new legal maxima; the page describes further testing and work toward action levels.
5.relevance: This is surveillance evidence for HMTc’s watch, with a preparation basis that must match any comparison. It is neither a threshold change nor validation of every lot or HMTc’s commercial benefit.

evidence.note: Read introduction, market-basket purpose/limitations, interpretation and the four element summaries, including the as-prepared-for-feeding basis. Arsenic speciation was assessed only in a subset. Separate human-milk data are limited to one donor bank and not representative nationally. Linked spreadsheets and all individual sample rows were not independently analyzed. The source does not substantiate a precise calendar of every 2026 agency deliverable.

6.referenceTitle: FAO/WHO: Codex Alimentarius Commission adopts new standards at CAC48
6.citation: FAO/WHO. FAO-WHO 48th Session of the Codex Alimentarius Commission adopts new standards. FAO Newsroom, November 10, 2025; session November 10–14, 2025.
6.summary: The official adoption report identifies new lead maxima of 2.5 mg/kg for dried bark spices and 2.0 mg/kg for dried culinary herbs, to be added to CXS 193-1995.
6.establishes: This verifies adoption by Codex for two defined food categories. It does not establish a separate national implementation date, a universal all-spice maximum, or a requirement that every country adopt these values.
6.relevance: It supplies an international benchmark event for HMTc’s watch. Market-access comparisons still require the destination’s applicable law and precise commodity, and Codex adoption does not itself change a certification threshold.

links.label: FAO/WHO: Codex Alimentarius Commission adopts new standards at CAC48

evidence.note: Read publication/session metadata and the section on maximum levels for lead in spices and culinary herbs, including the stated values and planned addition to CXS 193. This is official adoption reporting, not an independent review of every provision of the final consolidated standard.

8.citation: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India. Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Amendment Regulations, 2026. Notification F. No. 01/SP-02/S&S/NotificationContaminants/2021-22, May 14, 2026. Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part III, Section 4, No. 327; CG-DL-E-25052026-272840. Effective December 1, 2026.
8.summary: The final amendment extends lead and cadmium pulse categories to pulse flours. For fish oils it applies an inorganic-arsenic maximum of 0.1 mg/kg: total arsenic below that value clears the screen; a value above it requires inorganic-arsenic testing.
8.establishes: The amendment is adopted but takes effect December 1, 2026. The pulse changes expand product scope rather than publishing new numerical pulse limits. Total arsenic is a screen, not the regulated fish-oil species.
8.relevance: This provides a dated, adopted future rule in HMTc’s worldwide watch: December 1, 2026. Its species-specific fish-oil screen and pulse-flour scope expansion must be kept distinct from a generic reduction in all metal limits.

9.citation: Ministry of Health, Vietnam. Circular 12/2024/TT-BYT of July 18, 2024, promulgating QCVN 20-1:2024/BYT on contaminant limits in health supplements/dietary supplements. Official Gazette 895–896, August 5, 2024; effective August 1, 2025.
9.summary: Table 1 sets total arsenic 5, inorganic arsenic 1.5, lead 10 and mercury 0.5 mg/kg or mg/L. Cadmium is 3 for supplements containing seaweed or bivalve ingredients and 1 otherwise. Inorganic arsenic is checked when total arsenic exceeds 1.5.
9.establishes: The binding supplement rule includes product scope, transition terms and a conditional cadmium tier. Registered products made before commencement can continue to expiry under stated conditions; this is not a limit for every food.
9.relevance: This is an in-force supplement-limit event with transition terms and ingredient-dependent cadmium treatment. HMTc’s claimed stricter mapped cells need a separate comparison of the published program values against these exact species and mg/kg or mg/L bases.

10.citation: MERCOSUR Subgroup of Work No. 3. MERCOSUL/SGT N° 3/ATA Nº 03/25, 93rd ordinary meeting on Technical Regulations and Conformity Assessment, August 26–29, 2025. Portuguese official minutes, §2.3.
